items.title: Types Five Through Eleven: Faculties, Temperaments, and Leisure Revisited

items.zh: 云何中根補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，於所知事、所緣境界，所有諸根少遲運轉。一切如前，應當廣說。是名中根補特伽羅。云何利根補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，於所知事、所緣境界，所有諸根不遲運轉、與不微劣運轉。或聞所成、或思所成、或修所成作意相應。謂或信根，或精進根，或復念根，或復定根，或復慧根，有所堪能、有大勢力通達法義，速證真實。是名利根補特伽羅。云何貪行補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，於可愛事、可染著事所緣境界，有猛利貪、有長時貪。是名貪行補特伽羅。云何瞋行補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，於可憎事、可瞋恚事所緣境界，有猛利瞋、有長時瞋。是名瞋行補特伽羅。云何癡行補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，於所知事、所緣境界，有猛利癡、有長時癡。是名癡行補特伽羅。若生無暇、若有縱逸、若有邪行、若有障礙補特伽羅，如是一切如前應知。與此相違，應知即是生於有暇、無有縱逸、無有邪行、無有障礙補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a person with moderate faculties? It is such a person for whom, regarding what is to be known and the objects of contemplation, all the faculties operate somewhat slowly — everything else should be understood at length exactly as stated for weak faculties. This is called a person with moderate faculties. What is a person with sharp faculties? It is such a person for whom, regarding what is to be known and the objects of contemplation, all the faculties operate without slowness and without feebleness … having capacity, having great power, penetrating the meaning of the Dharma, swiftly realising what is genuinely true. This is called a person with sharp faculties. What is a greed-dominant person? It is such a person who, towards agreeable and attachment-inducing objects, has intense craving and long-lasting craving. This is called a greed-dominant person. What is a hatred-dominant person? …intense ill will and long-lasting ill will. This is called a hatred-dominant person. What is a delusion-dominant person? …intense delusion and long-lasting delusion. This is called a delusion-dominant person. Whether born without leisure, heedless, following wrong conduct, or obstructed — all of this should be understood exactly as stated before. Whatever is opposed to this should be understood as, precisely, being born with leisure, free of heedlessness, free of wrong conduct, and unobstructed.

items.title: Distant, in Two Different Senses: Time Still to Pass, and Effort Not Yet Begun

items.zh: 云何名遠補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，由時遠故，去涅槃遠；或有復由加行遠故，說名為遠。云何名為由時遠故，去涅槃遠？謂有如是補特伽羅，經多百生，或多千生，多百千生，然後方能值遇勝緣，得般涅槃。云何名為加行遠故，說名為遠？謂有如是補特伽羅，唯住種姓，而未趣入，不能速疾值遇勝緣、得般涅槃，彼於涅槃未能發起勝加行故。由加行遠說名為遠，不由時遠。
items.en: What is called a "distant" person? It is such a person who, because of temporal distance, is distant from nirvāṇa; or, again, such a person who, because of distance in practice, is called "distant." …It is such a person who, only after passing through many hundreds of lifetimes, or many thousands of lifetimes, or many hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, is then finally able to encounter the superior condition and attain nirvāṇa. …It is such a person who abides in lineage alone, not yet having entered, unable to swiftly encounter the superior condition and attain nirvāṇa, precisely because that person has not yet given rise to any excellent practice directed towards nirvāṇa at all. It is called "distant" because of distance in practice, not because of temporal distance.

items.zh: 如是二種總略為一，說名為遠補特伽羅。

items.title: Near, in the Same Two Senses — and Ripened Versus Unripened, Defined by the Body That Will Carry It

items.zh: 云何名近補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，由時近故，去涅槃近；或有復由加行近故，說名為近。云何名為由時近故，去涅槃近？謂有如是補特伽羅，住最後生、住最後有、住最後身，即由此身當得涅槃。或即由此剎那無間，於煩惱斷當得作證。如是名為由時近故，去涅槃近。云何名為由加行近說名為近？謂有如是補特伽羅，安住種姓，亦已趣入。如是二種總略為一，說名為近補特伽羅。云何未成熟補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，未能獲得最後有身。謂住於此能般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。是名未成熟補特伽羅。云何已成熟補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，已能獲得最後有身。謂住於此能般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。是名已成熟補特伽羅。
items.en: What is called a "near" person? It is such a person who, because of temporal nearness, is near to nirvāṇa; or, again, such a person who, because of nearness in practice, is called "near." …It is such a person who abides in the final rebirth, the final state of existence, the final body — by means of this very body, that person will attain nirvāṇa. Or, again, such a person for whom, in this very moment, without interruption, the cutting off of the afflictions is about to be realised. …It is such a person who abides in lineage and has already entered [the path]. These two, taken together in brief, are called a "near" person. What is an unripened person? It is such a person who has not yet obtained the final body of existence — the body in which nirvāṇa is attained, or in which one enters correct nature free of afflictive arising. This is called an unripened person. What is a ripened person? It is such a person who has already obtained the final body of existence — the body in which nirvāṇa is attained, or in which one enters correct nature free of afflictive arising. This is called a ripened person.

items.title: Section: The Twenty-Three Types Close — the Entire Ground of Spiritual Lineage Complete

items.zh: 云何未清淨補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，未生聖道，於聖道果煩惱離繫未能作證。是名未清淨補特伽羅。云何已清淨補特伽羅？謂與上相違，應知其相。如是名為安住種姓補特伽羅所有差別。為度彼故，諸佛世尊出現於世。謂若未趣入，令其趣入；若未成熟，令其成熟；若未清淨，令其清淨；轉正法輪，制立學處。
items.en: What is a purified person? It is such a person whose marks should be understood as opposite to those just described [for the impure]. These, then, are called the differences among persons who abide in lineage. It is precisely in order to liberate such beings that the buddha-bhagavats appear in the world: those not yet entered, they cause to enter; those not yet ripened, they cause to ripen; those not yet purified, they cause to be purified; turning the wheel of the true Dharma, and establishing the points of training.

blocks.text: The rest of the twenty-three types, which close the Stage of Lineage. These temperaments return later, when the treatise matches meditation objects to people.

Moderate and sharp faculties follow the weak. Then five dominant temperaments: greed, hatred, delusion, pride, discursive thought; plus the balanced and those of slight affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: everyone has greed, hatred, and delusion, but "when one is especially strong, we call the person greed-type". The first craving is "intense"; repeated, it becomes "long-lasting". Venerable Miào Jìng distinguishes ill will (intending harm) from mere dislike.

Far from nirvāṇa in two senses: **time** (many lives must still pass before meeting the right conditions; Venerable Miào Jìng: only after so long does one meet the Dharma, meet the Buddha) and **practice** (effort not yet begun).

Near, in the same two senses. **Ripened** means that this body is the one in which liberation will occur: the final existence, approaching the diamond-like concentration (Master Cháng Bǎi). "Entering the certainty of correct nature" (入正性離生): the noble path, free of the "rawness" of afflictions, or, on a second reading, free of birth in the lower realms.

subs.head: Purified; the Stage of Lineage complete

blocks.text: "Purified" persons are those from stream-entry to arhatship (Venerable Miào Jìng). With this, the first part of the Śrāvaka Stage is complete.
These categories are not ranks to compare oneself with others. They are a map, meant to help a teacher, or oneself, see what kind of help is needed now.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi say the greed, hatred, and delusion types are distinguished?
options: everyone has all three, but whichever is especially strong names the type
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in fact everyone has greed, hatred, and delusion, but when one affliction is especially strong, we call the person greed-type, hatred-type, or delusion-type.

quiz.q: The greed-dominant person has "intense craving and long-lasting craving." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish them?
options: the first craving is intense; the second, third, and countless after become long-lasting
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first craving is intense craving; the second, third, and countless times after become long-lasting craving. Everyone has greed, hatred, and delusion; whichever is especially strong names the type.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish "ill will" from mere "dislike"?
options: ill will intends to harm the other; dislike is only displeasure, without intent to harm
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: ill will means intending to harm the other; dislike is merely displeasure without any intent to harm.

quiz.q: In what two senses does the treatise call a person "distant"?
options: temporal distance — many hundreds of thousands of lives before meeting the superior condition; distance in practice — only in lineage, not yet entered, no excellent practice begun
quiz.why: "Because of temporal distance, distant from nirvāṇa; or, again, because of distance in practice, called distant." Master Cháng Bǎi: one is distance from the fruit of the path, the other distance from the path itself.

quiz.q: The note says the "temporally distant" person has in fact already begun genuine practice. How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: only after hundreds of thousands of lives does one meet the superior condition, meet the Dharma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: only after such a long time does he meet the excellent condition — meet the Dharma, meet the Buddha. The treatise likewise says "only after passing through many hundreds of lifetimes… is then finally able to encounter the superior condition"; the note's claim of practice already begun has no basis.

quiz.q: "正性離生" is rendered "correct nature free of afflictive arising." How do the masters explain 離生?
options: correct nature is the noble path; 離生 is freedom from birth in the lower realms after seeing cessation; the English takes only the "free of affliction" reading
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: second interpretation — correct nature is the noble path, and 離生 is freedom from life in the three lower realms. Venerable Miào Jìng: having seen the truth of cessation, one is free of the lower realms and will not fall into them — hence 離生.

quiz.q: The note narrows "purified" to arhatship. What range do the masters give?
options: from stream-entry through arhatship; one who has not attained the path is unpurified
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: from stream-entry up to the fourth fruit, the arhat — that is called a purified person; one who has not attained the path is not yet purified. Master Cháng Bǎi: buddhas appear to liberate beings of all three lineages, not only śrāvakas.
